records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/group/GroupTest.java:153 — [confidence 100][P2][advisory] When `managedRealm.admin().groups().group(groupUuid).remove();` throws, execution skips `deletedAll.set(true);` and leaves the untracked non-daemon reader in `while (!deletedAll.get())` issuing requests and retaining exceptions beyond test teardown, burdening subsequent tests and preventing normal JVM shutdown; the strongest rebuttal is that deletion succeeds on the happy path, but failure during a concurrency regression is precisely when cleanup must stop and join the reader in a finally block.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a real defect in the test code. Looking at lines 145-157, the reader thread runs `while (!deletedAll.get())` and `deletedAll.set(true)` is only called after the forEach loop that deletes groups. If any deletion throws an exception, `deletedAll.set(true)` will never execute, leaving the reader thread running indefinitely. Additionally, there's no `join()` call to wait for the thread to complete, and no finally block to ensure cleanup. This is a legitimate bug that could cause test pollution and resource leaks.
